cards.spanish: Being FROM a place (Soy de Colorado)
Being AT a place (Estoy en la oficina)
ser bueno = good person | estar bien = feeling fine
ser listo = smart | estar listo = ready
ser rico = wealthy | estar rico = delicious
ser vivo = clever | estar vivo = alive
a, de, por, para, con + infinitive
Use 'a' before people (Visito a mis padres)
No tengo nada = I don't have anything
un + masc noun; una + fem noun; uno stands alone (no noun after)
20s contract into one word: veintiuno, veintidós (y → i)
Use 'y' between: treinta y uno, cuarenta y dos
ciento veinte, ciento uno (no 'y' between hundred and the rest)
cien stands alone (100); ciento precedes another number (101 = ciento uno)

cards.english: a la una vs a las
cards.spanish: Use 'a la una' for 1 o'clock; 'a las' for all other hours
All days of the week are masculine — use el/los
el lunes = on Monday (one time); los lunes = on Mondays (recurring)
Nouns ending in -ión are feminine: la reunión, la lección
If a word ends in a consonant, add -es to pluralize (reunión → reuniones)
Add -mente to form adverbs: usualmente, normalmente, constantemente
In Spanish you talk WITH a person: 'hablar con' (not 'hablar a')
When a sentence begins with a noun, include the article: 'El café está listo'
